The quote command now prints **27.06** instead of 26.09, and all 7 tests pass.

**Root cause:** `to_cents` in `shop/money.py:9` padded a one-digit decimal with a zero on the wrong side. `"5".rjust(2, "0")` gives `"05"`, so `"12.5"` was read as 1205 cents ($12.05) instead of 1250. Two of those plus 8.25% tax came to 26.09. Any price with a single decimal digit was affected, so the bug wasn't limited to this one quote.

**Fix:** I changed `rjust` to `ljust`, so `"5"` becomes `"50"`. Prices with two decimals (`"12.05"`), no decimals (`"12"`) or a trailing dot (`"12."`) still convert correctly. The tax math was already right: 2 × 1250 = 2500, plus 8.25% tax (206) = 2706.

**Test:** I added `test_to_cents_single_decimal` to `tests/test_pricing.py`. It checks `"12.5"`, `"12.05"` and `"12"`.

The package has no `shop/__main__.py`, so `python3 -m shop quote ...` won't run yet. I tested with your `python3 -c` fallback. I haven't committed anything.
